_note: Lane-cited dictionary entries — standard classical Arabic meanings for high-frequency JA tokens in Saadia's Tafsir. Hand-curated against the corpus; not auto-generated. `source: "lane"` means "this is the standard classical Arabic sense, for which Lane's Lexicon is the canonical English reference" — entries paraphrase, they are not verbatim Lane quotes. For Saadia-specific or Blau-divergent senses, see data/tafsir-divergence.json. For tribute and Blau-citation policy, see /about/blau.
_source: Lane's Lexicon (E.W. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, 1863-1893; public domain). Roots verified against the Perseus TEI edition at ~/Tools/arabic-lexicon/lane-xml.
_scope: Hand-curated 2026-05-21; first batch ≈70 entries focused on top-frequency tokens from the Bereshit-Devarim corpus that are NOT in tafsir-divergence.json. Inflected surface forms (suffixed prepositions, fa-prefixed perfects) included where they appear ≥100x in the corpus to improve tap-to-define UX without yet extending the prefix/suffix-stripping logic in lib/lookup.ts.

then, thereupon, afterward

O! (vocative, calling out)
I
you (m.sg)
rather; on the contrary; nay

also, too, likewise

after; following; afterward
with, alongside, in the company of
from; about, concerning; away from
in front of, before, ahead of

is not; there is not

entries.gloss_en: land, country, region; town, settled place
entries.notes: Saadia frequently uses بلد where the Hebrew has ארץ in the sense of a specific land or region.

entries.gloss_en: year
people, folk, tribe, kinsmen
man (adult male); also: foot, leg (vocalized rijl)
entries.notes: Vocalization disambiguates: rajul "man" vs. rijl "foot". In Tafsir narrative, "man" is the dominant sense.

entries.gloss_en: matter, command, affair, order; (as verb) commanded, ordered
entries.notes: Same JA spelling for both noun amr and perfect verb amara — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: tent (of wool, hair, or skin); dwelling
entries.notes: Saadia's standard rendering of אהל.

entries.gloss_en: altar; place of slaughter or sacrifice
entries.notes: Standard rendering of מזבח.

entries.gloss_en: mountain, mount
human being, person; mankind
place, location, spot
house, dwelling; tent; household
king, sovereign
gold; (as verb dhahaba) he went, departed
entries.notes: Homograph: dhahab "gold" and dhahaba "went" share the JA spelling. Context disambiguates.

ten (10)
seven (7)
my hand; hand(s) (oblique/dual form of yad)
entries.notes: Surface form ידי = yad + 1sg suffix OR dual oblique "two hands". Lemma yad is "hand".

entries.gloss_en: was, became; existed
entries.notes: Most common copula in Tafsir narration: "And there was…". 3rd-person m. perfect.

entries.gloss_en: to make, fashion, fabricate, do
said, spoke (3sg.m. perfect)
spoke to, addressed (Form II); also: word, speech (kalim)
saying (m.sg., circumstantial)
entries.notes: Saadia's standard rendering of Hebrew לאמר when speech is reported.

entries.gloss_en: Israel (the patriarch, and the people descended from him)
Moses
entries.notes: Final yod marks Arabic alif maqṣūra (ى).

entries.gloss_en: Aaron
Egypt (the land); also: a frontier city
Jacob
Pharaoh (title of Egyptian kings)
Joseph
Abraham
to them; for them (m.pl.)
entries.notes: li- ("to, for") + -hum (3m.pl. suffix).

entries.gloss_en: in/with/by it; in/with him (3m.sg.)
entries.notes: bi- ("in, with, by") + -hi (3m.sg. suffix).

entries.gloss_en: in/with/by it; in/with her (3f.sg.)
entries.notes: bi- + -hā (3f.sg. suffix).

entries.gloss_en: in it; in him (3m.sg.)
entries.notes: fī ("in") + -hi (3m.sg. suffix).

entries.gloss_en: upon him/it; on it (3m.sg.)
entries.notes: ʕalā ("on, upon") + -hi (3m.sg. suffix).

entries.gloss_en: from him/it (3m.sg.)
entries.notes: min ("from") + -hu (3m.sg. suffix).

entries.gloss_en: from her/it (3f.sg.)
entries.notes: min + -hā (3f.sg. suffix).

entries.gloss_en: and he said; so he said (3sg.m. perfect of qāla)
entries.notes: fa- ("and / so") + qāla ("said"). The most common JA narrative tag.

entries.gloss_en: to, toward, until, up to
to, for, belonging to (proclitic preposition)
entries.notes: The preposition ل- prefixes onto the following word. Standalone surface forms (with pronominal suffix) are listed as variants. The bare letter ל is also a verbal modal prefix ('that he should'), context-dependent.

entries.gloss_en: lord, master; the Lord (God)
entries.gloss_he: אדון, רב; ה' (כאשר מיודע או מסומך)

entries.gloss_en: father, ancestor; (pl. ābāʔ) forefathers
entries.notes: Oblique stem before pronominal suffixes is أبي- (אבי-): אביה 'her father', אבוה 'his father' (nominative أبوه).

entries.gloss_en: except, but, save (introducing an exception)
who, which, that (f. sg.)
entries.notes: Feminine counterpart of اَلَّذِي / אלד'י. Plural forms: alladhīna (אלד'ין m.pl.), allātī (אללאתי f.pl.).

entries.gloss_en: they (m. pl.)
you (m. pl.)
people, family, household, kin; inhabitants (of a place)
door, gate, entrance
tribe (esp. of Israel); grandson, descendant
entries.notes: Saadia's stock rendering of Hebrew שבט when designating one of the twelve tribes. For 'rod/staff' Saadia uses قَضِيب / קצ'יב.

entries.gloss_en: thousand (1,000); (pl. ālāf) thousands
sanctity, holiness; (with article: al-quds) the sanctuary, the holy precinct
entries.notes: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מקדש / קדש (the Tabernacle's most holy region) is אלקדס.

entries.gloss_en: dwelling, abode; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מִשְׁכָּן) the Tabernacle
offering, oblation, sacrifice (that which is brought near)
entries.notes: Standard Saadianic rendering for Hebrew קרבן and for the 'pleasing aroma' (ריח ניחוח) — see the divergence card for קרבאן (Gen 8:21) where Saadia uses 'pleasing offering' instead of 'pleasing aroma' to avoid divine olfaction.

entries.gloss_en: Isaac (son of Abraham; second patriarch)
entries.notes: Saadia retains the Hebrew form יצחק throughout the Tafsir; standard Arabic إسحاق is given here for orientation.

entries.gloss_en: Esau (son of Isaac; ancestor of Edom)
Canaan (the land; also the son of Ham)
other, another; (al-ākhir) the last, the latter
thing, anything; (in negation) nothing
days (broken plural of yawm)
nation, community, people
age, era, lifetime; perpetuity, lasting time
wilderness, desert, open country; dry land (vs. sea)
entries.notes: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew מדבר. The same consonants spell barr 'pious / dutiful' and bīrr 'righteousness' — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: army, host, troops; military camp
silver, silver coin
twenty (20)
spouse, mate, pair; (in context) wife
god, deity (with article 'al-' → 'the God' = Allāh)
entries.notes: The root of אללה (Allāh, 'the God'). Saadia uses אלאה for אלהים when not referring to the unique God of Israel.

entries.gloss_en: end, last part, latter portion
entries.notes: Homograph with آخَر 'other' (above); same consonants, different vocalization.

entries.gloss_en: Moab (son of Lot; the Moabite nation east of the Jordan)
entries.notes: Saadia retains the Hebrew form מואב throughout the Tafsir.

entries.gloss_en: Abram (Abraham's name before Gen 17:5)
entries.notes: The pre-covenantal name of the first patriarch (renamed Abraham in Gen 17:5). Saadia uses אברם through Gen 17 and אברהים thereafter.

entries.gloss_en: Judah (fourth son of Jacob; the tribe and territory bearing his name)
entries.notes: Saadia retains the Hebrew form throughout.

entries.gloss_en: Rachel (Jacob's wife; mother of Joseph and Benjamin)
entries.notes: Homograph with the verb רחל 'to depart, journey' (root r-ḥ-l) — context disambiguates. Saadia retains the Hebrew form.

entries.gloss_en: he departed, journeyed, decamped (a tribe moving from one stopping place to the next)
entries.notes: Saadia's regular gloss for Hebrew נסע ('journey'); see Gen 12:9, Num 33:* repeatedly. Homograph with the proper noun רחל (Rachel) — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: the Jordan (river); the trans-Jordan region
entries.notes: Saadia's standard rendering of Hebrew יַרְדֵּן. The Arabic form al-Urdunn takes the definite article in nearly all attestations.

entries.gloss_en: Reuben (firstborn of Jacob; the tribe of Reuben)
Simeon (second son of Jacob)
Levi (third son of Jacob; the Levite tribe)
entries.notes: Saadia uses לוי for the patriarch; the gentilic 'Levite' appears as אלליואני (sg.) / אלליואניין (pl.).

entries.gloss_en: Issachar (ninth son of Jacob)
Zebulun (tenth son of Jacob)
Dan (fifth son of Jacob; the tribe of Dan and its northern territory)
entries.notes: Saadia identifies the place-name Dan with Banyas (see Gen 14:14). Homograph with the verb دَانَ 'to judge' (root d-w/y-n); here strictly the proper name.

entries.gloss_en: Naphtali (sixth son of Jacob)
Gad (seventh son of Jacob; the tribe of Gad)
Asher (eighth son of Jacob)
entries.notes: Homograph with the Arabic relative pronoun الذي and with the Hebrew relative אשר — Saadia uses אלד'י for the latter, so here the form is purely the proper name.

entries.gloss_en: Benjamin (twelfth son of Jacob; youngest, full brother of Joseph)
Manasseh (firstborn son of Joseph; one of the two Joseph tribes)
Ephraim (second son of Joseph; one of the two Joseph tribes)
Edom (Esau's other name; the Edomite nation)
Leah (Jacob's first wife; mother of six tribes and Dinah)
Laban (Jacob's father-in-law; brother of Rebekah)
entries.notes: Homograph with لَبَن 'milk' (same letters) — context disambiguates. The latter is rare in the Tafsir narrative chapters but appears in dietary contexts.

entries.gloss_en: Sarah (Abraham's wife; matriarch)
entries.notes: Saadia retains the Hebrew form. Homograph with the JA spelling of سار 'he walked' + ـه — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: Sinai (the mountain of revelation; the surrounding wilderness)
Balaam (son of Beor; the seer hired by Balak; Numbers 22-24)
Balak (king of Moab in the Balaam narrative)
Sodom (the city destroyed in Gen 19)
Eleazar (son of Aaron; high priest after Aaron's death)
he came down, descended, alighted; (in Saadia's gloss) the standard rendering of Hebrew יָרַד
he passed, went by, traversed (a place); (in Saadia's gloss) regular rendering of Hebrew עָבַר
entries.notes: Homograph with مُرّ 'bitter' (different vocalization). The verb root is m-r-r (gemination) — surface forms double the final ر.

entries.gloss_en: he entered, went in; (in Saadia's gloss) regular rendering of Hebrew בָּא (when 'enter') and similar
he went out, came forth, departed; (in Saadia's gloss) regular rendering of Hebrew יָצָא
going out, outside, exterior; (often used as adverb) outwardly, externally
entries.notes: Active participle of خَرَجَ; Saadia uses both as a substantive ('the outside, the exterior') and adverbially ('outside, outwardly'). Distinct from the verbal lemma כ'רג above.

entries.gloss_en: he carried, bore, lifted up; (in Saadia's gloss) frequent rendering of Hebrew נָשָׂא
he took, seized, received; (in Saadia's gloss) regular rendering of Hebrew לָקַח
he gathered, collected, brought together; (in Saadia's gloss) regular rendering of Hebrew אָסַף or קָבַץ
he dwelt, settled, resided; (in Saadia's gloss) regular rendering of Hebrew יָשַׁב 'to dwell'
entries.notes: Distinct from the noun מסכן 'Tabernacle' (same root, different form).

entries.gloss_en: it is incumbent, it is obligatory, it must (be done)
entries.notes: Saadia's standard impersonal modal for Hebrew constructions of obligation.

entries.gloss_en: appointed gathering-place, place of presence; (Saadia's gloss for אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד) the Tent of Meeting
entries.notes: One of Saadia's signature renderings: Hebrew אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד 'tent of meeting' becomes אלמחצ'ר '(the place of) presence/gathering'. Used hundreds of times across Shemot, Vayikra, and Bamidbar.

entries.pos: verbal noun (mas.dar of Form II kallama)
entries.gloss_en: act of speaking-with, addressing in speech; (often adverbial) 'in speech, by way of speech'
entries.notes: Saadia's adverbial-accusative 'תכלימא' renders Hebrew constructions where God explicitly speaks 'face to face' or 'mouth to mouth' (e.g. Num 12:8; Deut 5:4), reinforcing that the verb of speaking has a real object — the divine word reaches the human ear without intermediary. Cognate accusative pattern (he speaks a speaking).

entries.gloss_en: Egyptian (m. sg.); (broken pl.) the Egyptians
entries.notes: Gentilic of מצר (Egypt). Saadia regularly uses the broken plural אלמצריון for the collective.

entries.gloss_en: assembly, congregation, group, community; (Saadia's gloss for עֵדָה) the community of Israel
entries.notes: Saadia's regular rendering of Hebrew עדה. Distinct from גמע (the verb 'to gather').

entries.gloss_en: child, son, boy; (broken pl. awlād) children, sons
entries.notes: Saadia uses both ולד 'child/son' (sg.) and the broken plural אולד/אולאד. Distinct from the verb ולד 'to give birth' (root w-l-d) which is in form ولد and inflects on its own pattern — but they share the root.

entries.gloss_en: name, appellation; (broken pl. asmāʾ) names
entries.notes: Standard Arabic word for 'name'. Saadia uses both the singular אסם and the broken plural אסמא extensively (esp. in genealogies and the 'list of names of the sons of Israel' formulae).

entries.gloss_en: blood; (pl. dimāʾ) bloods, the blood (of multiple)
oil, grease, fat; (Saadia's gloss for שֶׁמֶן) anointing oil; fat of an animal
brother; (oblique stem before pronominal suffix: akhī-); (broken pl. ikhwa, ukhuwwa) brothers
entries.notes: Oblique stem before pronominal suffixes is أخي- (אכ'י-): אכ'יך 'your brother', אכ'יה 'his brother'. Nominative אכ'וך 'your brother'. The broken plural in Saadia is regularly אכ'ות (إِخْوَة 'brotherhood'), suffixed: אכ'ותה 'his brothers'.

entries.gloss_en: head; top, summit, beginning; chief, leader; (pl. ruʾūs)
entries.notes: Saadia uses ראס both literally (the head of a body) and metaphorically (the head/leader of a tribe, the top of a mountain).

entries.gloss_en: garment, robe, cloth, clothing; (broken pl. thiyāb) garments, clothes
entries.notes: Saadia's regular rendering of Hebrew בֶּגֶד and שִׂמְלָה.

entries.gloss_en: burnt offering, 'that-which-goes-up'; (Saadia's gloss for עֹלָה) the wholly burnt sacrifice
entries.notes: Saadia's signature rendering of עֹלָה — 'the one that goes up' (from ṣaʿada 'to ascend'), the wholly-consumed altar offering. The Hebrew is morphologically the same idea (עלה 'to go up'); Saadia preserves the semantic motivation.

entries.gloss_en: unit of weight, mithqāl; (Saadia's gloss for שֶׁקֶל) shekel-weight
entries.notes: Saadia's standard rendering for the Hebrew shekel as a weight-unit. Appears widely in legal-economic and tabernacle-construction passages.

entries.gloss_en: round, circular, spherical; rounded
entries.notes: Form X active participle of d-w-r. Saadia uses this for round objects in the tabernacle and altar specifications, and for round/encircling geographic descriptions.

entries.gloss_en: town, village, settlement
entries.notes: Saadia's standard rendering for both Hebrew עִיר and קְרִיָּה.

entries.gloss_en: well-being, soundness, safe-arrival, peace; (Saadia's gloss for שָׁלוֹם in greetings and well-wishes) safety, welfare
month; (pl. ashhur) months
sheep and goats, small cattle, flock; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew צֹאן) the flock
desert, wilderness, open uncultivated country
entries.notes: An alternate to בר 'wilderness' (which is more frequent in Saadia for מדבר); צחרא covers a more general sense of 'open country' or 'flat desert plain'.

entries.gloss_en: woman, wife; (Saadia's gloss for אִשָּׁה in non-pl. contexts) the woman/wife
entries.notes: Suppletive plural is נסא (nisāʾ) — see the נסא entry. Saadia uses the singular אמראה (with definite article אלאמראה) for 'the woman' and the suffixed form אמראתה 'his wife'.

entries.gloss_en: women, wives (suppletive plural of אמראה / اِمْرَأَة)
goats (collective); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עִזִּים) the goats
clan, kindred, tribal subdivision; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מִשְׁפָּחָה) family-clan
entries.notes: Saadia's standard rendering for Hebrew מִשְׁפָּחָה in tribal/genealogical contexts (esp. Num 26, Num 33, Josh 7).

entries.gloss_en: firstborn, first-issue, first of its kind; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בְּכוֹר) the firstborn
entries.notes: Saadia's regular rendering of Hebrew בכור. Distinct from the verb بَكَرَ 'to be early'.

entries.gloss_en: custom, statute, decree, prescribed mark; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew חֹק) statute, decreed practice
entries.notes: Saadia's regular rendering of Hebrew חֹק 'statute, decree' in legal contexts.

entries.gloss_en: behold, here is, this is (emphatic 'behold-this'); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הִנֵּה and הִנֵּה זֶה)
entries.notes: A fixed combination of the pronoun هُوَ 'he' + the near-demonstrative ذَا 'this' = 'he is this / behold him'. Saadia uses it pervasively for Hebrew הִנֵּה. Distinct from הד'א (this, m. sg.) — هَوَذَا is the emphatic-presentative form.

entries.gloss_en: length, duration; (with genitive) throughout, all of, for the duration of
entries.notes: Saadia uses טול both as a noun ('the length of X') and as a quasi-preposition: 'טול אלסנה' (throughout the year), 'טול עמרה' (all the days of his life). For Hebrew כֹּל when expressing temporal extent.

entries.gloss_en: such, thus, like-this; (in narrative) so-and-so, such-and-such
entries.notes: Fixed compound of כַ 'like' + ד'א 'this'. Distinct from the dictionary's existing entry כד'אך 'like that' (kadhāka).

entries.gloss_en: there, in that place (distant); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שָׁם)
entries.notes: Fixed adverb of place (distal). Distinct from ההנא 'here' (proximal).

entries.gloss_en: here, in this place (proximal); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew פֹּה and הֲלוֹם)
entries.notes: Fixed adverb of place (proximal). Compound of הא 'lo' + הנא 'here'. Distinct from הנאך 'there'.

entries.gloss_en: and upwards, henceforth, from-that-point-and-onwards; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew וָמַעְלָה 'and above')
entries.notes: Frozen adverbial form built from fa- 'and' + ṣāʿidan 'ascending'. Saadia's regular rendering of Hebrew וָמַעְלָה in census formulae (e.g. 'from twenty years and upwards').

entries.gloss_en: cause, reason, means, occasion; (bi-sabab) because of
entries.notes: Saadia uses 'בסבב' (literally 'in [the] cause of') as the regular preposition for Hebrew בִּגְלַל and בַּעֲבוּר. Compare also 'מן אגל' as an alternative.

entries.gloss_en: hand; arm; power, possession; (dual yadayn / pl. aydī)
entries.notes: Note: the lemma 'ידי' (yadī, 'my hand' or oblique stem before suffixes) is already in the dictionary with its own variants. This entry adds the bare singular יד and the broken plural אידי / אלאידי.

entries.gloss_en: thirty (30)
forty (40)
fifty (50)
sixty (60)
seventy (70)
three (f.) / three (m. thalatha = ת'לאת'ה)
two (oblique form of اِثْنَان); (in pair-construction) 'two of...'
six (f.) / six (m. sitta = סתה)
bitter; (as noun) bitterness, myrrh-like bitter substance
entries.notes: Homograph with the verb مَرَّ 'he passed' (above) — same consonants, different vocalization. The two are kept as separate entries to flag the ambiguity for readers.

entries.gloss_en: milk; (in Saadia) the substance 'milk'
entries.notes: Homograph with the proper noun לבן (Laban) — see the separate entry. Context disambiguates: dietary/zoological contexts vs. patriarchal-narrative contexts.

entries.gloss_en: elder, old man, chief, sheikh; (broken pl. shuyūkh / mashāyikh) elders
entries.notes: Saadia's rendering of Hebrew זָקֵן in the elder-of-the-community sense.

entries.gloss_en: middle, midst; (with genitive) in the midst of, among
entries.notes: Saadia's regular rendering of Hebrew תּוֹךְ in the prepositional sense 'in the midst of'.

entries.gloss_en: side, flank, region, direction; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew צַד and פֵּאָה in directional contexts)
time, moment; (as temporal conjunction) when, at the time when
entries.notes: Saadia uses חין both as a noun ('a time') and as a temporal connector ('when'). Distinct from וקת which is a more general 'time' word.

entries.gloss_en: wood, timber, planks (collective); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עֵץ in lumber/construction contexts)
cubit (unit of length); forearm; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אַמָּה in measurements)
unclean, ritually impure; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew טָמֵא)
entries.notes: Saadia's signature gloss for the ritual-purity term טָמֵא. The verb ינגס 'becomes impure' is its denominative imperfect.

entries.gloss_en: covenant, pact, pledge; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בְּרִית)
morning, early daytime; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בֹּקֶר)
great, mighty, immense, magnificent; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew גָּדוֹל)
entries.notes: In JA, this root is sometimes spelled עצ'ים (with ṣād + dot) instead of עט'ים — both spellings represent the same Arabic letter ظ (ẓāʾ). Both surface forms are listed as variants.

entries.gloss_en: bone; (broken pl. ʿiẓām) bones; the essence, substance of a thing
entries.notes: Same root as עט'ים 'great' (above) — bones being 'the great/strong parts'. Saadia's rendering of Hebrew עֶצֶם.

entries.gloss_en: consecrated, sanctified, made-holy; (as noun, with article) the Sanctuary, the Tabernacle precinct
entries.notes: Passive participle of qaddasa (Form II: 'to consecrate'). Distinct from the noun קדס 'sanctity / the Sanctuary' (already in dict) — מקדס is the participial form.

entries.gloss_en: fire, flame; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֵשׁ)
entries.notes: Same root as נור 'light' (n-w-r) — distinct lexeme. נאר is feminine, ניראן is the broken plural.

entries.gloss_en: beast, animal (esp. quadruped, domesticated or wild); (broken pl. bahāʾim) beasts
entries.notes: Saadia's standard rendering of Hebrew בהמה.

entries.gloss_en: chest, ark, box; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֲרוֹן in 'ark of the covenant')
entries.notes: Saadia's regular rendering of Hebrew אֲרוֹן for the ark of the covenant. Also applies to Noah's ark (Hebrew תיבה).

entries.gloss_en: servant, slave, worshipper; (as verb) he served, worshipped, was-subject-to
entries.notes: Saadia uses עבד both for the noun (Hebrew עֶבֶד) and the verb (Hebrew עָבַד). Homograph kept as one entry since both senses share the same root and inflectional pattern.

entries.gloss_en: he went up, ascended; (in Saadia) regular rendering of Hebrew עָלָה
entries.notes: Same root as צעידה 'burnt offering' (above) — the offering that 'goes up' in smoke.

entries.gloss_en: presence, immediate vicinity; (bi-ḥaḍrati X) in the presence of X, before X
entries.notes: Same root as מחצ'ר 'gathering-place' (above). Saadia uses 'בחצ'רה' as a prepositional locution for Hebrew לִפְנֵי 'before' (esp. before God or a person of rank).

entries.gloss_en: he placed, set, made, appointed; (in Saadia) regular rendering of Hebrew שָׂם / נָתַן in 'place/appoint' contexts
is it? does? (introducing a yes/no question)
substitute, exchange, replacement; (as preposition) instead of, in place of
mighty hero, strong warrior, chief; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew גִּבּוֹר in heroic contexts)
he slaughtered, sacrificed; (as noun) slaughter, sacrifice, slaughtered-animal
he seeks forgiveness, pleads for pardon, atones; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew יְכַפֵּר 'atone')
entries.notes: Form X yastaghfir of root g-f-r ('to cover, forgive'). Saadia's standard rendering of the Hebrew piʿel יְכַפֵּר 'he will atone' in priestly-atonement contexts.

entries.gloss_en: he died, expired, passed away; (in Saadia) regular rendering of Hebrew מֵת
gift, bestowed portion, inheritance; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נַחֲלָה)
entries.notes: Saadia preserves the Hebrew form נחלה (which already exists in Arabic as nihla 'gift, bequest'). The Arabic root n-ḥ-l 'to give as a free gift' aligns semantically with the Hebrew inheritance term.

entries.gloss_en: body, trunk; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בָּשָׂר and גְּוִיָּה in many contexts)
entries.notes: Distinct from the divergence card for בדן (Gen 3:21, where it covers a more pointed semantic move). Here the bare noun and its inflections.

entries.gloss_en: ram; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אַיִל in sacrificial contexts)
he gave, bestowed, granted; (in Saadia) regular rendering of Hebrew נָתַן
entries.notes: Saadia's signature rendering of Hebrew נָתַן. Form IV (causative-like) of the root ʿ-ṭ-w 'to extend, hand over'.

entries.gloss_en: male, male animal; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew זָכָר)
entries.notes: Saadia uses ד'כר for the bare Hebrew זָכָר 'male'; the broken plural ד'כוה / ד'כור appears in census contexts. 'לאלד'כוה' = 'for the males'.

entries.gloss_en: water (variant spelling of the existing מא entry; here a fuller plene spelling)
entries.notes: Alternative orthography of the JA 'water' word. Already in dict as מא (with the same gloss); this entry adds the plene spelling מאא that appears in some scribal traditions.

entries.gloss_en: object of worship, deity, idol; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֱלִיל and גִּלּוּלִים) the false god
entries.notes: Saadia's anti-idolatry signature: rather than translating Hebrew elilim as 'gods' (which would dignify them), he uses the participle 'objects of worship' — sidestepping any implication of real divinity.

entries.gloss_en: sin, fault, offense, error; (as verb) he sinned, erred
(the) Responder, one who answers; (Saadia's gloss for divine epithets meaning 'God who hears')
entries.notes: Saadia uses 'אלמג'יב' as a divine epithet, often paired with 'אלטאיק' (the All-Capable) in liturgical-prayer contexts within Tafsir.

entries.gloss_en: (the) All-Capable, the One Who Has Power; (Saadia's divine-name rendering, esp. paired with אלכאפי for Hebrew אֵל שַׁדַּי)
entries.notes: Component of Saadia's compound divine name 'אלטאיק אלכאפי' (the All-Capable, the Sufficient) — his rendering of Hebrew אֵל שַׁדַּי. See the divergence cards on Bereshit 17 for context.

entries.gloss_en: (the) Sufficient, the One Who Suffices; (Saadia's divine-name rendering — see טאיק)
above, over, on-top-of; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מֵעַל and עַל in 'over/above' senses)
copper, bronze; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נְחֹשֶׁת)
noble, of-high-rank, eminent; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נָדִיב and נִכְבָּד)
nobles, men-of-rank; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים in Gen 6 — the 'sons of the noble class')
entries.notes: Broken plural of שריף. Already discussed under tafsir-divergence (Gen 6:2, 6:4: 'sons-of-the-nobility' for בני האלהים). Add as standalone lemma so the bare form resolves outside the divergence-card flow.

entries.gloss_en: he chooses, selects, picks-out; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בָּחַר)
entries.notes: Form VIII (reflexive-derived) of خ-ي-ر 'good/excellent' → 'to pick the best'. See the divergence card for אכ'תיאר (Gen 4:7) for the noun/abstract form.

entries.gloss_en: he called, summoned, read-aloud; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קָרָא in 'call' and 'read' senses)
entries.notes: Direct Saadia rendering of Hebrew קָרָא — the cognate carries over.

entries.gloss_en: outer canopy, hanging-cloth screen; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קֶלַע — the courtyard hangings of the Tabernacle)
entries.notes: Persian-origin loanword in Arabic, used by Saadia for the screen-fabric panels of the Tabernacle courtyard. Heavy in Exodus 27-38.

entries.gloss_en: acacia (wood); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שִׁטִּים — the wood of the Tabernacle)
weight; weighing; (as verb wazana) he weighed-out; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שָׁקַל and מִשְׁקָל)
the (definite article); (as standalone) the article in isolation, typically a citation form or break in text
entries.notes: Normally proclitic: prefixes onto a noun. The standalone form is rare and usually a citation or text break.

entries.gloss_en: he becomes unclean, contracts impurity; (Saadia's denominative of nájisun 'unclean')
entries.notes: Denominative imperfect built on the adjective נגס 'unclean' (see the נגס entry). High-frequency in Vayikra purity laws.

entries.gloss_en: he found, came-upon, discovered; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מָצָא)
crimson, kermes-red dye; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי) the scarlet/crimson tabernacle thread
sky-blue, azure (Persian-loan color term); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew תְּכֵלֶת)
entries.notes: Persian asmān 'sky' + gūn 'color' → 'sky-colored'. Saadia's signature rendering of the tabernacle's blue thread.

entries.gloss_en: he killed, slew; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הָרַג and הִכָּה לְמָוֶת)
Amorite (one of the Canaanite peoples)
time, point-in-time, appointed-moment; (broken pl. awqāt) times
entries.notes: The bare singular waqt — companion to the existing אוקאת (the broken plural). Saadia uses both.

entries.gloss_en: behold me, here am I; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הִנֵּנִי and הִנֵּה אֲנִי)
entries.notes: Compound of demonstrative ها 'behold' + 1sg pronoun אנא. Saadia's rendering of Hebrew הִנֵּנִי.

entries.gloss_en: he counted, enumerated, took census; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew סָפַר, פָּקַד, נָשָׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ in census contexts)
petty chief, lesser leader (diminutive of raʾīs); (Saadia's nuanced rendering of secondary tribal-leadership terms)
entries.notes: Diminutive of رئيس 'chief'. Saadia uses this form to differentiate junior leadership (e.g. heads of sub-clans) from the principal נשיא.

entries.gloss_en: cloud, cloud-cover; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עָנָן)
religious community, religion, creed; (in Saadia) used for circumcision-covenant community contexts
entries.notes: Saadia uses millah (and its derivatives) in contexts of religious-community identity; appears in covenant-circumcision narratives.

entries.gloss_en: he ate, consumed; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אָכַל)
food, sustenance; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֹכֶל)
pure, ritually clean; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew טָהוֹר)
raised, lofty, exalted; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew רָם and גָּבוֹהַּ)
pleasing, agreeable, acceptable; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew רָצוֹן and לְרָצוֹן in offering contexts)
vessels, utensils (collective); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew כֵּלִים in cultic-utensil contexts)
young he-goat; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עַתּוּד — Hebrew form retained)
lord, master, sir; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֲדוֹנִי in human-respect contexts; NOT for the divine Name)
entries.notes: Saadia uses סייד for human masters and respected superiors (e.g. אדני in interpersonal contexts). For the divine Name יהוה Saadia uses אללה.

entries.gloss_en: we (1pl)
(the) Eternal, the Self-Sufficient One; (Saadia's divine-name rendering in some contexts; mostly an epithet)
entries.notes: An Arabic divine epithet (also in the Qurʾan, Surat al-Ikhlāṣ); Saadia uses it sparingly in his theological prose.

entries.gloss_en: the Nile (river); (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew יְאֹר and פִּישׁוֹן)
entries.notes: Geographic identification long established in Saadia: יְאֹר (and elsewhere פִּישׁוֹן) = the Nile.

entries.gloss_en: he made-stand, set-up, established, raised-up; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הֵקִים)
entries.notes: Form IV (causative) of qāma 'to stand'. Saadia's regular rendering of the Hebrew hiphil הֵקִים.

entries.gloss_en: leader, commander, prince; (Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נָשִׂיא)
to draw near, come close, touch (something)
entries.notes: Form I. In Saadia's purity laws (Num 19) consistently means 'touch/come near to' a corpse. Root دنا / دنو.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. دنا: 'دَنا من الشيء دنُوّاً ... قَرُبَ' (drew near); also lane s.v. dnw confirms 'he was, or became, near'

entries.gloss_en: go! proceed! (imperative of مضى)
entries.notes: Imperative of مضى Form I. Contexts: Num 22:20 'arise, go with them'; Num 22:35 'go with the people'; Gen 12:1 'go from your land'. The form אמץ' = iMDi (imperative). Apostrophe marks ض (ḍad).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. مضى: 'maDaY He ... passed; went; or went away' and 'imperative xu*o' pattern

entries.gloss_en: purple-crimson cloth or dye
entries.notes: Arabicized loan from Persian argawān (red-flowered tree). Lane r0.xml: 'ArjwAn … intensely red; red garments'. Used in Saadia's Tafsir to render Hebrew אַרְגָּמָן (purple/crimson).
entries._grounding: lane r0.xml s.v. أرجوان: 'intensely red; red garments or clothes'

entries.gloss_en: leprosy; white skin disease
entries.notes: Lane: 'baraSN ... a whiteness which appears upon the exterior of the body'. Used throughout Lev 13 for the skin-disease rendering Hebrew צָרַעַת. The ץ = ص (ṣad).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. برص: 'baraSN ... a certain disease ... a whiteness incident in the skin'

entries.gloss_en: take! (imperative of أخذ)
entries.notes: Imperative of أخذ Form I; Lane: 'imperative xu*o'. The כ' marks خ (khā'); ד marks ذ (dhāl). Surface וכד also represents the same imperative with wāw prefix.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أخذ: 'A^xa*a ... imperative xu*o, originally A@w^oxu*o'

entries.gloss_en: you (pl.) eat / you shall eat
entries.notes: 2mp imperfect of أكل. Lane: 'A^akalahu ... He ate it'. The inflected form covers negated contexts (Gen 3:3 'do not eat thereof') and affirmative (Gen 45:18 'you shall eat').
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أكل: 'A^akalahu ... He ate it, namely, food'

entries.gloss_en: curtain, veil (of the Tabernacle)
entries.notes: Lisan: 'السَّجْفُ والسِّجْفُ: السِّتْر'. Used by Saadia to render the Tabernacle parokhet/veil in Ex 26:33, Num 4:5, Num 18:7.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. سجف: 'السَّجْفُ والسِّجْفُ: السِّتْر' (the curtain/veil)

entries.gloss_en: Kadesh; Saadia's Arabic name for Kadesh-Barnea
entries.notes: Saadia consistently uses רקים to render the biblical place-name קָדֵשׁ (Kadesh/Kadesh-Barnea); Num 20:1, 20:14, 13:26. The Arabic رقيم (raqīm) means 'inscribed/written' and was a known geographic name. Not a Lane entry for this toponym.
entries._grounding: Blau does not attest this toponym; Lane has رقم s.v. 'He wrote', but the proper-noun use is Saadia's rendering of קדש

entries.gloss_en: a sojourner who has entered the community; resident alien
entries.notes: Blau: 'neophyte, convert, proselyte / הנכנס לדת'. In Saadia's Num 15 contexts, אלג'ריב אלדכ'יל renders 'the sojourner who sojourns among you'. The apostrophe marks خ (khā').
entries._grounding: blau s.v. دخيل: 'neophyte, convert, proselyte / הנכנס לדת'

entries.gloss_en: with/to you (pl.); concerning you
entries.notes: Preposition بـ with 2mp pronominal suffix كم. Lane attests بِكُم as standard compound. Num 14:28 'as you have spoken before Me'; Num 33:56 'as I planned to do to them, so I will do to you'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. بـ (preposition): بِكُمْ = 'with/to you (plural)' — standard pronominal compound

entries.gloss_en: he lived, passed his life (a number of years)
entries.notes: 3ms perfect of عاش (Form I of عيش). Lane: 'EaA$a He lived'. Contexts: Gen 11:11–13 'and he lived after that N years'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عيش: 'EaA$a ... He lived; he passed life in a particular manner'

entries.gloss_en: offer! present! (pl. imperative, of sacrifice)
entries.notes: Form II imperative of قرب (qarraba = to bring near, offer). Lane qrb s.v. 2: 'He brought [it] near'. Blau also attests Form II 'to be sacrificed (offerings)'. Used throughout Num 28 for making burnt offerings.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قرب Form II: 'He brought near'; blau s.v. قرب Form II: 'to be sacrificed (offerings)'

entries.gloss_en: Aram (biblical region/people = Arameans)
entries.notes: Biblical proper noun: Aram/Arameans (Heb. אֲרָם). Saadia transcribes ארם directly. Lane has آرام as arabicized form of the name. Appears Gen 10:23, Gen 22:21, Num 23:7.
entries._grounding: proper noun transcription; Lane has no entry for this toponym, but standard Arabic form is آرام

entries.gloss_en: wild animals, beasts of the field
entries.notes: Lisan: 'الوَحْش: كلُّ شيء من جواب البَرّ مما لا يَسْتأْنس' (every creature of the wilderness that is not domesticated). Used Gen 1:25, 1:30, 2:19 to render חַיַּת הַשָּׂדֶה/חַיַּת הָאָרֶץ.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. وحش: 'كلُّ شيء من جواب البَرّ مما لا يَسْتأْنس' (wild land animals)

entries.gloss_en: he counted, enumerated, took a census of
entries.notes: Form I of عدّ. Lisan: 'العَدُّ: إِحْصاءُ الشيءِ، عَدَّه ... عَدّاً وتَعْداداً' (counting, enumeration). Num 26:63–64: 'those whom Moses and Aaron counted (عدا) among Bnei Yisrael'. Root doubled-د.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. عدد: 'العَدُّ: إِحْصاءُ الشيءِ، عَدَّه يَعُدُّه عَدّاً'

entries.gloss_en: our father
entries.notes: أب 'father' with 1cp suffix -نا (our). Num 27:3–4 'our father died'; Gen 19:31 'our father is old'. Standard Arabic morphology; Lane s.v. أبو.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ابو: أبونا = 'our father', nominal with first-person plural suffix

entries.gloss_en: desert, open wilderness
entries.notes: From بر (open country/land). Asas Zamakhshari confirms 'نزلوا بالبرية' = 'they camped in the wilderness'. Lisan s.v. بر. Used throughout Num to render מִדְבַּר.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. بر (open land) and asas-zamakhshari s.v. برية confirming 'wilderness'

entries.gloss_en: except, apart from, save (exception particle)
entries.notes: Used in construction ما خلا (mā khalā) = 'except'. Lane khw/khlw: 'xalaA commencing with xalaA as a word denoting exception'. Num 18:3, 28:23, 28:31: 'everything except the vessels of holiness'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. خلو (xalaA): 'xalaA as a word denoting exception'

entries.gloss_en: sound, whole, without defect (animals for sacrifice)
entries.notes: Acc./adv. form of صِحاح (sound, healthy). Lane s.v. صح: 'He was, or became, healthy, or sound; or restored to health'. Used Num 28:3,11,19 to qualify sacrificial lambs: 'without defect'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صح: 'SaH~a ... He was, or became, healthy, or sound'

entries.gloss_en: generations, progeny, lineage
entries.notes: Plural of تليد / abstract of ولد root. Lane s.v. ولد: 'wilaAdahN ... walaAdN'. In Saadia, consistently renders Hebrew תּוֹלְדוֹת in genealogical headings (Gen 10:1, 11:10, 11:27) and census formulas (Num 1:20,22,24).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ولد: birth, generation, progeny

entries.gloss_en: he called out; summoned; prayed
entries.notes: Form I of دعا. Lisan: 'ادْعوا شُهداءكم ... اسْتَغِيثوا بهم'. Num 21:3 'God hearkened to the prayer/call of Israel'; Gen 12:8 'called out by His name'; Gen 20:8 'summoned all his servants'.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. دعا: 'الدُّعاءُ ... اسْتَغاثَ, سَأَل'

entries.gloss_en: cursed, accursed
entries.notes: Passive participle of لعن. Lisan: 'رجل لَعِينٌ ومَلْعُونٌ'. Gen 3:14 'you are cursed above all beasts'; Gen 27:29; Num 24:9: 'those who curse you shall be cursed'.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. لعن: 'رجل لَعِينٌ ومَلْعُونٌ ... اللَّعْنُ: الإِبْعادُ والطَّرْد من الخير'

entries.gloss_en: chest, coffer; the Ark of the Covenant
entries.notes: Lane s.v. صندق: 'SunoduwqN ... A chest, coffer, or trunk'. In Saadia: consistently renders אֲרוֹן הָעֵדוּת (Ark of the Testimony/Covenant). Lisan confirms: 'الصُّنْدوق: الجُوالِق'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صندق: 'SunoduwqN ... A chest, coffer, or trunk'

entries.gloss_en: the priests (Saadia's term for the Kohanim)
entries.notes: Blau: 'إمام ... not only leader but mainly priest / לא רק מנהיג בכלל, אלא בעיקר כהן'. Saadia uses this to render כֹּהֵן (priest) and כֹּהֲנִים throughout the Tafsir.
entries._grounding: blau s.v. إمام: 'not only leader but mainly priest / כהן'

entries.gloss_en: war, battle
entries.notes: Lane s.v. حرب. Standard classical Arabic: the noun حَرْب (war, battle). Blau also confirms Form I 'to wage war'. Num 10:9 'if you go to war'; Num 24:20 'first in war among nations'; Num 31:14 'returning from battle'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حرب: 'Harabahu ... He despoiled him'; lane lists noun حَرب (war) throughout the entry

entries.gloss_en: and take! (imperative of أخذ with wāw)
entries.notes: ו + imperative خُذْ (from أخذ). Same lemma as כ'ד (id: khud-take-imperative); listed separately because the surface וכד lacks the apostrophe variant. Same root, same meaning.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أخذ: imperative xud

entries.gloss_en: gainful work, labor for gain
entries.notes: Verbal noun of pattern mafʿal from كسب (to gain/earn). Lane s.v. كسب: 'He collected [wealth]; he gained, acquired, or earned'. Phrase 'כל צנעה' מכסב' = 'every work of gain/earning' in festival laws (Num 28:18, 25, 26) renders מְלֶאכֶת עֲבֹדָה.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. كسب: 'kasaba ... He gained, acquired, or earned, wealth'

entries.gloss_en: aromatic resins/gums (used as incense)
entries.notes: Plural of صَمْغ. Lisan: 'الصَّمْغُ ... شيء يَنْضَحُه الشجر ويَسيل منها' (what exudes and flows from trees = gum). Blau: 'resin / קרף'. Used for בְּשָׂמִים/סַמִּים (spices/incense) Ex 25:6, 30:7, Num 4:16.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. صمغ: 'شيء يَنْضَحُه الشجر' (gum/resin); blau s.v. صمغ: 'resin / קרף'

entries.gloss_en: accept, receive (favors, offerings, or intercession)
entries.notes: Form I of قبل. Lane: 'qabila He took, received, or admitted, willingly, or with approbation; he accepted'. Num 16:15 'do not accept their offering'; Num 27:20 'so the community will accept him'; Deut 13:9 'do not listen to him'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قبل: 'qabila He took, received ... with approbation; he accepted'

entries.gloss_en: stranger, foreigner; one who is not native
entries.notes: Adjective used as noun. Lane s.v. غرب: 'garaba ... He became [a stranger, a foreigner; or] far, or distant, from his home'. In Saadia, renders גֵּר (sojourner) in Num 15, Gen 17:12. Apostrophe marks غ (ghayn).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. غرب: 'garaba ... He became a stranger, a foreigner'

entries.gloss_en: to permit, allow, give leave (to do something)
entries.notes: Form IV imperfect passive/active of طلق. Lane s.v. طلق Form IV: 'ATlq lahu fiEola ka*aA He permitted him, or gave him permission or leave, to do such a thing'. Gen 41:34; Gen 43:14; Deut 18:14.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. طلق Form IV: 'ATlq lahu ... He permitted him, or gave him permission or leave'

entries.gloss_en: my soul; myself; my own accord
entries.notes: نفس + 1cs suffix. Lane: 'nafasN ... soul, spirit, self, person'. 'ליס מן תלקא נפסי' (Num 16:28) = 'not of my own accord'. 'ותחיא נפסי' (Gen 12:13) = 'my soul will live'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. نفس: 'nafsN ... The soul; the spirit; self'

entries.gloss_en: stretched out (his hand), extended
entries.notes: fa- (then/so) + 3ms perfect مَدَّ (Form I of مدد). Lisan: 'المَدُّ: الجَذْب والمَطْلُ. مَدَّه يَمُدُّه مَدّاً' (stretching out). Gen 19:10 'the men stretched out their hands'; Gen 22:10; Gen 48:14 'Israel stretched out his right hand'.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. مدد: 'المَدُّ: الجَذْب والمَطْلُ. مَدَّه يَمُدُّه مَدّاً'

entries.gloss_en: stood, halted, stopped (in a place)
entries.notes: Form I perfect/imperative of وقف. Lane: 'waqafa He was, or became, still, or stationary; he stood still; he continued standing'. Also used as imperative 'قف' = stand/stop. Num 22:24; Num 23:3, 15.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. وقف: 'waqafa He was, or became, still, or stationary; he stood still'

entries.gloss_en: Joshua (son of Nun)
entries.notes: Biblical proper noun; Saadia renders יְהוֹשֻׁעַ as יהושע (Hebrew letters, unchanged). Num 11:28, 13:16, 14:6. Not a dictionary entry.
entries._grounding: proper noun; no lexicon entry needed

entries.gloss_en: the liver
entries.notes: Lane s.v. كبد: 'kabid [or liver]'. Standard classical term. Ex 29:13,22: 'the lobe of the liver' (זאידה' אלכבד). Deut 4:11: 'to the heart/midst of the heaven' (כبد السماء).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. كبد: 'kabadahu ... He ... hit, or smote, or hurt, his kabid [or liver]'

entries.gloss_en: your dwelling, your household
entries.notes: منزل + 2ms/2mp suffix. Lane s.v. نزل: manziluN = 'a place of alighting, or abiding; a dwelling-place, house'. Num 18:11,13: 'every clean person in your household may eat it'; Deut 11:19.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. نزل: 'manzilN ... a place of alighting ... a dwelling-place'

entries.gloss_en: half
entries.notes: Lane s.v. نصف: 'AlnaSofN ... one of the two halves of a thing'. Num 12:12 'half his flesh eaten away'; Num 15:10; Num 28:14 'half a hin for each bull'. The ץ = ص (ṣad).
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. نصف: 'النِّصْفُ: أَحد شقَّي الشيء' (one half of something)

entries.gloss_en: male goats (dual), two he-goats
entries.notes: Dual of عَتُود (a young he-goat ready for mating). Lane s.v. عتد: 'Eatuda ... It (a thing) was, or became, ready, at hand'. The noun عَتُود / عَتِيد means 'prepared/ready male goat'. Num 7:17,23,29 etc.: 'five he-goats' (five of عتدان in the texts).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عتد: the noun 'Eatwdap' (young male goat) within the entry

entries.gloss_en: uncover, expose, reveal (genitals or nakedness)
entries.notes: Form I of كشف. Lane: 'ka$afahu He uncovered it; unveiled it; laid it open; displayed it; exposed it to view'. Gen 9:21 'exposed himself in his tent'; Ex 20:23 'lest you expose your nakedness'; Lev 18:7.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. كشف: 'ka$afahu He uncovered it; unveiled it; laid it open'

entries.gloss_en: in you; with you; against you (prep. بِ + 2 m.s. pronoun)
entries.notes: Fused preposition-pronoun; lemma בִּ (بِ) is s.v. Lane art. bA (prepositions).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. bA (bi-); pronoun suffix -ka standard Arabic; context: בלעם 22:28 מא צנעת בך

entries.gloss_en: in me; with me; against me (prep. بِ + 1 s. pronoun)
entries.notes: Fused preposition-pronoun; same lemma as בך with different suffix.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. bA (bi-); context: לא יומנון בי 14:11

entries.gloss_en: exclusive sacred things; special reserves; sancta
entries.notes: Plural of خاصّة; Lane s.v. خصص: 'he singled it out to the exclusion of others.' In the Tafsir always followed by אלאקדאס (the holy things), translating קֹדֶשׁ הַקֳּדָשִׁים.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. خصص: خصّه بالشيء ... أفرده به دون غيره; lane s.v. xSS

entries.gloss_en: other than; not; except
entries.notes: Indeclinable particle of exception; functions as negative adjective or preposition.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. gyr: particle denoting 'other than, not, except'

entries.gloss_en: Lot, son of Haran, nephew of Abraham
entries.notes: Biblical figure; Hebrew לוֹט. Lane s.v. lwT notes lūṭ as a proper name.
entries._grounding: proper noun; biblical equiv. Hebrew לוֹט; context: bereshit 11:27 אולד לוט

entries.gloss_en: between me (prep. بَيْن + 1 s. pronoun suffix)
entries.notes: Fused preposition-pronoun; always in the phrase ביני ובינך/ובינכם.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. byn: bayn = 'between'; context: יחכם אללה ביני ובינך 16:5

entries.gloss_en: her year; its (f.) year (as measure of animal age)
entries.notes: Genitive of سَنَة 'year' + 3 f.s. possessive; used of female sacrificial animals: רכ'לה אבנה' סנתהא = 'a ewe-lamb in its [first] year.'
entries._grounding: lane s.v. snh: sanah/sanah = 'a year'; context: bamidbar 6:14

entries.gloss_en: your fathers; your ancestors (2 m.s.)
entries.notes: Plural آباء of أب 'father' + 2 m.s. suffix; Lane s.v. Abw lists pl. آباء as the preferred form.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. Abw: pl. A=baA='N (آباء) 'fathers, ancestors'

entries.gloss_en: and he washes; bathes (his body)
entries.notes: wa- (و) + imperfect of رَحَضَ 'to wash (a garment or body)'; Lane s.v. rHD. JA apostrophe on ץ' marks ض (ḍād).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. rHD: raḥaḍa 'He washed … a garment … and his hand'

entries.gloss_en: Bashan, region east of the Jordan ruled by Og
entries.notes: Arabic rendering of biblical הַבָּשָׁן; Lane does not lemmatize as geographical; context always 'Og king of Bashan.' JA apostrophe on ת' marks ث.
entries._grounding: proper noun; biblical equiv. הַבָּשָׁן; context: bamidbar 21:33 עוג מלך אלבת'נייה

entries.gloss_en: so it intensified; became fierce or severe
entries.notes: fa- (ف) + form VIII اشتدّ of شدّ 'to be hard/intense'; Lisan s.v. شدد: فاشتدّ 'became intense, strong.' Lane lists the root under $d.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. شدد: شَدَّه ... فاشتدّ; context: פאשתד ג'צב אללה גדא 11:10

entries.gloss_en: Rebekah, wife of Isaac, daughter of Bethuel
entries.notes: Biblical proper name; Hebrew רִבְקָה; Lane does not have an entry for this name.
entries._grounding: proper noun; biblical equiv. Hebrew רִבְקָה; context: bereshit 22:23 ובתואל אולד רבקה

entries.gloss_en: incense; aromatic fumigant burned as an offering
entries.notes: Lane s.v. bxr: baxūr 'a substance burned for fumigation'; accusative ending -an in JA. JA apostrophe marks خ (kh).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. bxr: baxūr = substance used for fumigation/incense

entries.gloss_en: Heshbon, capital city of Sihon king of the Amorites
entries.notes: Biblical city name; Arabic transcription of Hebrew חֶשְׁבּוֹן; not in Lane as a geographical entry.
entries._grounding: proper noun; biblical equiv. Hebrew חֶשְׁבּוֹן; context: bamidbar 21:25

entries.gloss_en: a tenth part; tithe (one-tenth of an ephah as grain measure)
entries.notes: Lane s.v. E$r: Eu$orN 'a tenth, a tenth part, one part of ten parts.' In the Tafsir renders עִשָּׂרוֹן (the grain measure of one-tenth of an ephah).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. E$r: Eu$orN 'A tenth; a tenth part; one part of ten parts'

entries.gloss_en: amen; so be it (response to prayer or oath)
entries.notes: Lane s.v. Amn: A=miynaN 'amen, a word used at the end of a prayer or supplication.' Indeclinable.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. Amn: A=miyna / A^amiyna = amen after supplication

entries.gloss_en: the stranger; the alien; one far from home
entries.notes: Lane s.v. grb: gariyb 'a stranger, or foreigner; one who is far, or distant, from his home or native country.' Translates Hebrew גֵּר (sojourner).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. grb: gurubah/ghurbah 'the being far or distant from home'; gariyb = stranger

entries.gloss_en: for the sin-offering; as a purification sacrifice
entries.notes: Saadia uses زكوة/דכוה (classical: purity, alms) to render Hebrew חַטָּאת 'sin-offering'; attested in the Arabic transcript of Tafsir Num 6:14 لِلزَّكْوَةِ. Lane s.v. zkw gives 'purity' as a primary sense. This specific sacrificial application is Saadia's technical usage.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. zkw: zakaA = 'purity'; blau s.v. זכו: to gain/acquire. Arabic transcript Num 6:14 confirms לאלדכוה = لِلزَّكْوَةِ = לחטאת

entries.gloss_en: the open country; desert field; uncultivated plain
entries.notes: Lisan s.v. صحر: الصَّحْراء البَرِّيَّة 'the wilderness, the open country'; the trailing yā' in JA אלצחרי is the nisba or pausal yā'. Translates שָׂדֶה/הַשָּׂדֶה.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. صحر: الصَّحْراء = open field, wilderness, uncultivated country

entries.gloss_en: yesterday; recently
entries.notes: Lane s.v. Ams: 'Yesterday, or the day before the present day'; indeclinable adverb.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. Ams: A^amos = 'yesterday, or the day before the present day'

entries.gloss_en: at that time; thereupon; then
entries.notes: Compound حِين (time/when) + إذٍ (then); Lane s.v. Hyn: HIyn 'a time, a period of time.' The compound حينئذٍ means 'at that time.' JA spelling חיניד' drops the hamza.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. Hyn: HIyn = 'a time'; compound HiynayidhN = 'at that time'

entries.gloss_en: filled (with); full of
entries.notes: Passive participle (m. acc.) of مَلَأَ 'to fill'; Lane s.v. mlA^: malaA^a 'He filled a vessel'; mamlū' = filled. ממלוון is the dual m. form of the same word.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. mlA^: malaA^a 'He filled'; passive part. mamlū' = 'filled'

entries.gloss_en: large bowl; deep dish for offerings
entries.notes: Lane s.v. qSE: qaSoEap 'A bowl not so large as a jafnah … a wooden bowl.' In the Tafsir translates Hebrew קְעָרָה (the offering bowl) weighing 130 shekels.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. qSE: qaSoEah = 'A bowl … that satisfies ten; it is a wooden bowl'

entries.gloss_en: I swore; I took an oath; I vowed
entries.notes: Form IV perfect 1 s. of قَسَمَ; Lane s.v. qsm: A^aqosama Ealayohi 'He conjured him; he said biHaq~ika.' Saadia uses it for divine oath: אקסמת לאברהים ויצחק ויעקוב.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. qsm: A^aqosama 'He conjured; swore by'

entries.gloss_en: Horeb, the mountain of God (Sinai)
entries.notes: Arabic transcription of Hebrew חֹרֵב; Lane s.v. xrb treats خَرِب as 'ruined/desolate' but does not identify this as the place-name. Saadia uses חריב throughout Devarim for the mountain.
entries._grounding: proper noun; biblical equiv. Hebrew חֹרֵב; context: devarim 1:2 מן חריב

entries.gloss_en: Kohath, son of Levi, ancestor of the Kohathite clan
entries.notes: Biblical proper name; Hebrew קְהָת; Lane has no entry. The JA form is a direct transliteration.
entries._grounding: proper noun; biblical equiv. Hebrew קְהָת; context: bamidbar 3:17

entries.gloss_en: their father
entries.notes: أب 'father' (oblique أبي) + 3 m. pl. suffix; Lane s.v. Abw. Same root as אבאיך.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. Abw: ab 'father'; pl. suffix forms discussed

entries.gloss_en: hides; skins (of animals, used for coverings)
entries.notes: Plural of جِلْد 'skin, hide'; Lane s.v. jld: jilodN 'The skin of any animal; the integument of the body.' In the Tafsir: ג'שא גלוד דארש = 'a covering of dugong hide.'
entries._grounding: lane s.v. jld: jilodN 'The skin of any animal … pl. juluwd'

entries.gloss_en: he becomes; it turns into
entries.notes: Imperfect 3 m.s. of صَارَ; Lane s.v. Syr: SaAra 'He, or it, attained to the state or condition of such a thing; became such a thing.' Copular verb like كان.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. Syr: SaAra = 'He attained to the state of; became'

entries.gloss_en: Goshen, the region in Egypt settled by Jacob's family
entries.notes: Saadia's Arabic rendering of Hebrew גֹּשֶׁן (Goshen); Lane does not identify this as a place-name entry. The Arabic السَّدِير appears in Saadia consistently for Goshen.
entries._grounding: proper noun; biblical equiv. Hebrew גֹּשֶׁן; context: bereshit 45:10 בלד אלסדיר

entries.gloss_en: and he looked; and he gazed
entries.notes: fa- (ف) + perfect 3 m.s. of نَظَرَ; Lane s.v. nZr: naZara A_ilayohi 'He looked at, or towards, in order to see.' JA apostrophe on צ' marks ظ (ẓāʾ).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. nZr: naZara = 'He looked at or towards'

entries.gloss_en: he saw; he perceived; he observed
entries.notes: Perfect 3 m.s. of رَأَى 'to see'; the final alif in JA spelling marks the radical ى. Lane s.v. rAY.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. rAY: raA^aY 'He saw it'

entries.gloss_en: the giants; the mighty tyrants; the Anakim
entries.notes: Plural of جَبَّار; Lane s.v. jbr: jabbār 'Huge, tall, and strong; a giant' (tropical sense). Translates Hebrew עֲנָקִים (sons of Anak).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. jbr: jab~aArN 'Huge, tall, and strong; a giant'

entries.gloss_en: is found; there is; let there be found
entries.notes: Imperfect passive 3 m.s. of وَجَدَ (form IV passive يُوجَد or form I passive يُوجَد); Lane s.v. wjd: wajadahu 'He found it.'
entries._grounding: lane s.v. wjd: wajadahu 'He found'; passive yūjad = 'is found'

entries.gloss_en: the great one; the elder; the high priest
entries.notes: Lane s.v. kbr: kabura 'He was or became great.' In the Tafsir האמאם אלכביר = the High Priest (כֹּהֵן הַגָּדוֹל). Also used for the Great Sea (Mediterranean).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. kbr: kabura 'was or became great'; kabīr = great, big, senior

entries.gloss_en: your dwellings; your settlements
entries.notes: Plural of مَسْكَن 'dwelling, place of abode' + 2 m. pl. suffix; Lane s.v. skn: sakana 'It was, or became, still … and said of a man [dwelling/residing].'
entries._grounding: lane s.v. skn: maskan = 'dwelling, place of abode'

entries.gloss_en: the Sabbath; Saturday
entries.notes: Lane s.v. sbt: sabata 'He rested, and ceased or abstained from works'; AlsabtN 'the Sabbath; and Saturday.' Standard JA term.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. sbt: sabata = 'he rested'; AlsabtN = 'the Jewish Sabbath'

entries.gloss_en: unleavened bread; dough not allowed to rise
entries.notes: Lane s.v. fTr: faTiyrN 'Dough unleavened; or not left until it has become good; contr. of xamiyroN.' Also: Eiydu AlofaTiyri = Feast of Unleavened Bread (Passover).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. fTr: faTiyroN = 'dough unleavened'; contrasts with xamiyroN (leavened)

entries.gloss_en: come! (imperative m.s.); come hither
entries.notes: Imperative 2 m.s. of form VI of عَلَا; Lane s.v. Elw: 'Addressing a man … taEaAla, with fet-h to the l, originally meaning Be thou elevated … used in the sense of Come.' Frozen form regardless of gender/number in spoken usage.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. Elw: taEaAla = imperative 'come!' originally 'be elevated'

entries.gloss_en: she bore, gave birth to (a child)
entries.notes: Form I fem. 3sg. past; ولَّد (form II) = act as midwife. In context Saadia uses ولدت consistently for birth of named figures.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ولد (wld): 'She brought forth a child; She bore a child' — waladatu, inf. n. wilādah and walādah.

entries.gloss_en: twisted linen thread; fine twisted yarn
entries.notes: Passive participle of شَزَرَ 'to twist'; used in Tabernacle weaving contexts (Ex 26:1) parallel to Hebrew שֵׁשׁ מָשְׁזָר. Blau attests شزر = 'to twist' (citing Ibn Janāḥ).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شزر: $zr — to twist (thread); blau s.v. شزر (שזו): 'to twist'.

entries.gloss_en: dye; dyestuff (usually crimson dye)
entries.notes: صِبْغ (sibġ) = dye; in Saadia consistently as צבג' קרמז 'crimson dye' = תולעת שני. Lane: Sabagahu = 'he dyed it'. Blau: صبغ 'to be dyed / nrṭb'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صبغ (Sbg): 'He dyed it … a garment or piece of cloth'; blau s.v. صبغ (צבג): 'to be dyed / נצבע'.

entries.gloss_en: army, military force, troops
entries.notes: In Saadia גישה / גיוש = جَيْش 'army'. Lane: jy$ — 'assembled, armies, or military forces'. The form לגיושהם = لِجُيُوشِهِم 'for/in their armies'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. جيش (jy$): 'He collected, or assembled, an army, or a military force'; jayo$N = army.

entries.gloss_en: your localities, settlements, dwelling-places
entries.notes: Plural of مَحَلّ (maḥall) 'a place of abode, settlement' + 2ms suffix -ka; Lane: maHal~N = 'A place where a person or party alights … a place of alighting, or abode, or settlement'; pl. maḥāll. Saadia uses it for the localities/gates of Dt 12:17 etc.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حل (Hl): maHal~N … 'a place of alighting, or abode, or settlement … pl. maHaAl~u'.

entries.gloss_en: the right (side), right-hand
entries.notes: Fem. elative/superlative form of يَمِين; الْيُمْنَى = the right side. Lane: 'Alyamiynu * The location that is on the right.' Saadia: יד אלימני / אד'ן אלימני = right hand / right ear.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. يمن (ymn): 'Alyamiynu * The location that is on the right'.

entries.gloss_en: his heart (as seat of will, courage, emotion)
entries.notes: قَلْب (qalb) + 3ms suffix -hu. Lane: qalobN * = 'The heart'. Saadia: פשכך קלבה = 'his heart doubted/hesitated'; לא ירתפע קלבה = 'his heart shall not be lifted up'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قلب (qlb): 'qalobN * The heart; syn. fuw^aAdN'.

entries.gloss_en: or (disjunctive, in questions: 'which of the two?')
entries.notes: Disjunctive interrogative conjunction. Lane: 'A^amo * is a conjunction … It denotes interrogation … corresponding to the interrogative A^a … meaning A^aY~ … which of them two.' Distinct from أَوْ (aw). In Saadia: אהו שדיד אם מסתרכ'י = 'Is it strong, or lax?'
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أم (Am): 'A^amo * is a conjunction … It denotes interrogation … meaning A^aY~: which of the two?'

entries.gloss_en: your servants, your slaves (collective honorific)
entries.notes: عَبِيد = pl. of عَبْد 'slave, servant'; + 2ms -ka. Used in Saadia as a self-referential honorific plural when addressing a superior (Moses, God). Lane: 'He was, or became, a slave, or in a state of slavery'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عبد (Ebd): slave/servant — Eabada, EibaAdapN; EabiydN = slave; pl. EabiydN.

entries.gloss_en: he does, performs, carries out (a deed or act)
entries.notes: Form I imperfect 3ms; EamalaN = 'He worked, or wrought; he did, acted, or performed'. Saadia uses יעמל for 'shall do' (vow text) and for manual work.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عمل (Eml): 'Eamila … aor. Eamala, inf. n. EamalN, He worked, or wrought … he did, acted, or performed'.

entries.gloss_en: your companion, fellow, neighbor
entries.notes: صَاحِب (ṣāḥib) + 2ms -ka = 'your companion/associate'. Lane: SHb 1 = 'He associated, kept company, or consorted, with him … SAHibN = companion, associate, comrade, fellow, friend'. Blau attests a JA sense 'husband' (influenced by Heb. בעל) — but Saadia uses it in the standard classical sense of 'companion/neighbor'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صحب (SHb): 'SaHibahu … He associated, kept company, or consorted, with him … companion, associate, comrade, fellow, friend'.

entries.gloss_en: he released, let go, set free
entries.notes: Form IV of طَلَقَ. Lane: 'A^aTolaqa … He let go the captive; and set him free; he loosed the bond of the captive, and let him go'. In Gen 8:7 = שלח הערב; Gen 8:8 = שלח הת יונה.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. طلق (Tlq) form 4: 'ATlq AlA^asiyra … He let go the captive; and set him free; he loosed the bond'.

entries.gloss_en: the interior, inside, inner cavity (of body or structure)
entries.gloss_he: הפנים, חלל הפנים (של גוף או מבנה)
entries.notes: Lane: jawofN = 'It reached his jawof [or inside, or interior]'. In Saadia: אלשחם אלמג'טי אלגוף = 'the fat covering the cavity/interior', and אלמהג אלאוסט פי גוף אלתכ'אתג = 'the bar through the interior of the planks'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. جوف (jwf): 'jaAfatohu … jawofN [or inside, or interior, &c.]'; inf. n. jawofN = 'It reached his jawof'.

entries.gloss_en: their nobleman, chieftain, leader
entries.notes: شَرِيف (šarīf) = 'high, noble, possessing glory, honour, or nobility … the pl. is A^a$oraAfN and $urafaA^'. Saadia uses ושריפהם for the tribal chief named after each camp unit (Num 2).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شرف ($rf): '$ariyfN * High, elevated, exalted, or eminent … possessing glory, honour, dignity, or nobility; pl. A^a$oraAfN and $urafaA^'.

entries.gloss_en: and she named him, called him by the name
entries.notes: Form II 3fs past of سَمَّى (sm~Y) + 3ms suffix; Lane: 'sm~Y … He named him, or called him, Such a one; … he made [such] to be his name, his proper name.' In Saadia: ואסמתה ראובן = 'and she named him Reuben'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. سمو (smw) form II: 'sm~Y … teshdeed … He named him, or called him, Such a one'.

entries.gloss_en: gift, present sent as an act of courtesy or honor
entries.notes: Lane: 'hadiy~apN * [n. un.] A present; i.e. a thing sent to another in token of courtesy or honour'. In Gen 32:19: הד'א הדייה מבעות'ה לסיידי = 'this is a gift sent to my lord'. In Gen 4:3: הדייה ללה = 'an offering to God'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. هدي (hdy): 'hadiy~apN * A present; i.e. a thing sent to another in token of courtesy or honour'.

entries.gloss_en: he crossed over, passed across (a river, border)
entries.notes: Form I: Eabara = 'He passed, went, or crossed, over it … namely a river'. Also used as noun עבר = عِبْر 'the side/bank (of the Jordan)': Lane cites EiborN = 'the side of a river'. In Num 32 Saadia alternates verb and noun senses.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عبر (Ebr): 'Eabara bihi … He passed … from one side thereof to the other … a river'; also EiborN 'the side' of a river.

entries.gloss_en: a curtain panel, an oblong strip of cloth
entries.notes: Lane: '$aq~apN * primarily signifies The half of a garment … applied to an oblong piece; syn. sabiybapN musotaTiylapN … pl. $uqaqN and $iqaAqN.' In Ex 26:2 Saadia: כל שקה = 'each curtain strip'. Plural is שקאק = شِقَاق.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شق ($qq): '$aq~apN * primarily the half of a garment … an oblong piece … pl. $uqaqN and $iqaAqN'.

entries.gloss_en: the well (water-well)
entries.notes: بِئْر (bi'r) is classical Arabic for well (masc. in classical, often fem.); Lisan: 'البِئْرُ: القَلِيبُ، أُنثى، والجمع أَبْآرٌ'. Lane references biy^orN throughout. Saadia: אגמע אלקום ... אעטיהם מאא = 'assemble the people … I will give them water' (Num 21:16–18).
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. بأر: 'البِئْرُ: القَلِيبُ، أُنثى، والجمع أَبْآرٌ'; lane passim biy^orN 'A well'.

entries.gloss_en: the two tablets (stone), dual construct
entries.notes: لَوْح (lawḥ) = 'That [meaning a tablet] upon which one writes'. Dual لَوْحَيْ (lawḥay). Lane: 'lawoHN … That [a tablet] upon which one writes; katabonaA lahu fiY AlA^alowaAHi [We wrote … upon the tablets]'. Saadia: נחת לוחי גוהר = 'I hewed tablets of stone'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. لوح (lwH): 'lawoHN … That upon which one writes … (Kur vii. 142) AlA^alowaAHi [tablets]'.

entries.gloss_en: day of rest, holiday, cessation from work
entries.notes: Blau attests عُطْلَة = 'holiday, free day / יום פגרה' with explicit citation from Saadia's Tafsir on Lev 26:34. Lane has EuTolapN = 'the state of being without work, or occupation' but does not yield 'rest day'. Blau is the primary reference for the Saadia-specific sense.
entries._grounding: blau s.v. عطلة (עטלה): 'holiday, free day / יום פגרה'; citing Saadia Tafsir Lev (וס"ג לויקרא).

entries.gloss_en: a people, nation, tribe
entries.notes: Lane: '$aEobN * … A great number of people; … a tribe, or nation'. In Saadia consistently = עם/לאום: שעב מקדס ללה = 'a holy nation to God'; שעב כלבו יקום = 'a people, as a lion, shall rise'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شعب ($Eb): '$aEobN * A great number of people … a tribe or nation'.

entries.gloss_en: Gershon (son of Levi, head of Levitical clan)
entries.notes: Biblical proper name, Hebrew גֵּרְשׁוֹן, transliterated into Judeo-Arabic. No Arabic root. Appears throughout Num as the tribe responsible for carrying Tabernacle coverings.
entries._grounding: proper noun — Hebrew biblical name גֵּרְשׁוֹן, JA transliteration.

entries.gloss_en: he enters, comes into (service, assembly)
entries.notes: Form I imperfect 3ms of دَخَلَ (dakala). Standard classical Arabic. Lane: dakala = 'He entered; he came, or went, in, or into'. Saadia: ידכל לאלגיש = 'he enters into the army/service'; לא ידכל מפדוג' = 'an injured person shall not enter'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. دخل (dxl): 'daxala … He entered; he came, or went, in, or into'.

entries.gloss_en: for war, for battle, for combat
entries.notes: لِـ + الْحَرْب: Lane: 'HarobN Hrb War, battle, fight, or conflict; contr. of silomN'. In Saadia: לאלחרב = 'to/for battle' (Num 21:33; 32:27).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حرب (Hrb): 'HarobN Hrb War, battle, fight, or conflict; contr. of silomN'.

entries.gloss_en: springs (of water); also: eyes (dual/pl.)
entries.notes: Plural of عَيْن (ʿayn) = eye / spring of water. Lane: 'AlEayonu signifies The eye'; and 'maA^N maEiynN … Water of which one has reached the springs or sources'. Saadia uses עיון אלג'מר = 'the springs of the great deep' (Gen 7:11); also עיון אלגמאעה = 'inadvertence of the congregation' (lit. 'eyes = awareness').
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عين (Eyn): 'AlEayonu signifies The eye … pl. EuyuwnN (عيون)'; spring of water sense also attested.

entries.gloss_en: strong, mighty, severe, harsh
entries.notes: Fem. form of شَدِيد (šadīd). Lane: '$adiydN * strong, powerful, mighty'. In Saadia: יד שדידה = 'a mighty hand'; שדידה is the fem. agreeing with יد (hand) or referring to a force.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. شدد ($dd): '$adiydN * strong, powerful, mighty … بَيِّنُ الشِّدَّةِ'; lisan s.v. شدد: 'شيء شَدِيدٌ: مُشتَدٌّ قَوِيٌّ'.

entries.gloss_en: your land, your soil, your ground
entries.notes: أَرْض (arḍ) + 2ms -ka. Lane: 'A^aroDN * The earth … a land, or country'. The ḍ is represented by ץ' (with apostrophe for Arabic letter ض). In Saadia: אמץ' מן ארצ'ך = 'depart from your land' (Gen 12:1).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. أرض (A^rD): 'A^aroDN * The earth; a land, or country; a region; a tract'.

entries.gloss_en: Hagar (Egyptian maidservant of Sarah, mother of Ishmael)
entries.notes: Biblical proper name. Arabic هَاجَر (Hājar) is the standard Arabic form of Hebrew הָגָר. Lane does not have a dedicated entry for this name. Appears throughout Gen 16 in Saadia.
entries._grounding: proper noun — biblical Hebrew הָגָר; Arabic هَاجَر is the standard Arabic biblical form.

entries.gloss_en: a full measure of; enough to fill
entries.notes: مِلْء (mil') = 'the filling of a vessel; the amount that fills'. Lisan: 'مَلأَ الشيءَ يَمْلَؤُه مَلأً' = 'He filled the thing'. In Saadia: מל ביתה פצ'ה וד'הב = 'the full of his house of silver and gold' (Num 22:18); מל אלמכ'אזין = 'filling the granaries' (Gen 41:47).
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. ملأ: 'مَلأَ الشيءَ يَمْلَؤُه مَلأً … مِلْء = the filling / amount that fills'.

entries.gloss_en: a staff, rod, stick
entries.notes: عَصًا (ʿaṣā), originally عَصَوٌ. Lane: 'EaSFA * i.q. EuwdN [a staff, or stick, or rod]'. In Saadia Num 17: עצא עצא לכל בית אב = 'a staff for each ancestral house'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. عصو (ESw): 'EaSFA * i.q. EuwdN [as meaning A staff, or stick, or rod]'.

entries.gloss_en: craft, trade, skilled work, handiwork
entries.notes: Lane: 'SinaAEapN … the Hirofap [i.e. craft or handicraft, or a trade] … any habitual work or occupation'. In Saadia: ליעמל צנאעה פי כ'בא = 'to perform service in the Tent of Meeting'; לא תצנע פיה צנאעה = 'do not perform work in it'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. صنع (SnE): 'SinaAEapN … craft or handicraft, or a trade … any habitual work or occupation'.

entries.gloss_en: Shem (eldest son of Noah, ancestor of Semitic peoples)
entries.notes: Biblical proper name. Arabic سَام (Sām) = Hebrew שֵׁם. Standard transliteration in Islamic/JA tradition. Appears in Saadia's Gen 10 as the ancestor of the Semitic nations.
entries._grounding: proper noun — Hebrew שֵׁם; Arabic سَام is the standard Arabic biblical/Quranic form.

entries.gloss_en: with stones, by stoning
entries.notes: بِـ + الْحِجَارَة = 'with stones'. Lane: HajarN / HijaArapN = 'A stone; pl. HijaArapN'. Saadia: ירגמוהמא באלחגארה = 'they shall stone them with stones'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. حجر (Hjr): 'HajarN … A stone; pl. HijaArapN'.

entries.gloss_en: he rises, stands up; fulfills, carries out
entries.notes: Form I imperfect 3ms of قَامَ. Lane: 'qaAma … He rose, i.e. from sitting or reclining'. Saadia uses it in two senses: (a) physical 'he shall rise' (Num 23:24), (b) metaphorical 'carries out / fulfills' (Num 23:19: 'does he speak and not carry it out?').
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قوم (qwm): 'qaAma … He rose, i.e. from sitting or reclining; He stood up'.

entries.gloss_en: the (dining) table set with food
entries.notes: Lane: 'maAy^idapN * A table with food upon it; without food upon it, a table is not thus called, but is called xiwaAnN'. Saadia uses it for the Tabernacle shewbread table (Ex 25:23; Num 3:31).
entries._grounding: lane s.v. ميد (myd): 'maAy^idapN * A table with food upon it'.

entries.gloss_en: those who dwell, reside, are settled (in a place)
entries.notes: Active participle (form IV) of أَقَامَ 'to reside, settle'; pl. مُقِيمِينَ. Lane: 'muqiymN * Lasting; continuing … resident'. Saadia: אלקום אלמקימין פיה = 'the people who reside in it'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. قوم (qwm): 'muqiymN * Lasting, continuing … resident'; masc. pl. muqiymuwna/muqiymiynaA.

entries.gloss_en: nakedness, pudenda (as object of sexual prohibition)
entries.notes: سَوْأَة (saw'a) = pudendum, nakedness. Lisan: 'السَّوْأَةُ: الفَرْجُ … فالسَّوْأَةُ كلُّ عَمَلٍ وأَمْرٍ شائن'. Used in Saadia as the JA equivalent of Hebrew עֶרְוָה throughout Lev 18 incest prohibitions. Blau does not have a clear separate entry for saw'a in this sense.
entries._grounding: lisan s.v. سوأ: 'السَّوْأَةُ: الفَرْجُ. الليث: السَّوْأَةُ: فَرْج الرَّجل والمرأَة. قال اللّه تعالى: بَدَتْ لهما سَوْآتُهما'.

entries.gloss_en: then he returned, went back
entries.notes: فَ (then/so) + رَجَعَ (he returned). Lane: 'rajaEa … He returned; he went, or came, back'. The פ- prefix = Arabic فـ 'so, then'. Saadia: פרגע הרון אלי' מוסי = 'then Aaron returned to Moses'.
entries._grounding: lane s.v. رجع (rjE): 'rajaEa … He returned; he went, or came, back … he reverted; contr. of *ahaba'.
